name: Rue
waitingLines: I’m good. ...Just waiting on {partner}. Not like I care. ...I care a little.
I’ll stick around till {partner}’s back. Got nowhere to be. ...Are you okay?

questions.scene: Rue leans in your doorway, arms crossed. A tiny smile tries to escape. She stops it.
lines: I'm good. ...Are you? Cool. Quiz. Keep up.
questions.question: Why do wolves howl?

choices.label: Because they're sad
reply: Not always. Sometimes it's just 'hey.'
Howls are mostly for communication and finding the pack.
Happy howls exist. I don't do them. Often.

choices.label: To communicate and find their pack
reply: Correct. Good ears.
Howls help wolves find each other and mark territory over long distances.
Sky says my howl sounds like 'come home.' ...Whatever.

choices.label: At the moon, obviously
reply: Movie myth. The moon's not involved.
Wolves howl to find each other and talk across distance.
We just tilt our heads up. Sound carries better.

questions.factBasis: Wolves howl to communicate, assemble the pack, and mark territory.

questions.scene: Rue looks at a photo of a snow leopard and almost smiles. Almost.
lines: I'm good. ...This one's quiet. Like me. Respect.
questions.question: What can't snow leopards do, unlike lions and tigers?

choices.label: Roar
reply: Correct. No roar.
They chuff, hiss, and mew, but their throats can't make a true roar.
Quiet but deadly. Honestly? Goals.

choices.label: Climb
reply: They climb mountains for fun. Literally.
The thing they can't do is roar.
Instead they make a soft 'chuff.' Very low-key. I respect it.

choices.label: Jump
reply: They jump like it's nothing. Several times their body length.
What they can't do is roar.
Silent mountain cats. No drama. Just results.

questions.factBasis: Snow leopards cannot roar due to larynx anatomy.

questions.scene: Rue holds a mug of something warm, sipping slowly.
lines: Sharing question. Hard for me.
questions.question: What do vampire bats do for roost-mates who missed a meal?

choices.label: Ignore them
reply: Nope. They help.
They share regurgitated blood with hungry roost-mates.
Bats who share get help later. Trust, but make it bats.

choices.label: Teach them to hunt better
reply: Not quite.
They share food directly, by regurgitating blood.
Friends who share, get shared with. It's a system.

choices.label: Share regurgitated blood with them
reply: Correct. Gross. Kind.
Bats share meals with roost-mates who couldn't feed, and those friends return the favor.
Relying on others to survive. ...I'm learning.

questions.factBasis: Vampire bats share regurgitated blood with roost-mates; reciprocity is observed.

questions.scene: Rue squints at a zebra photo for a long time.
lines: I'm good. ...Trying to find two the same. Can't.
questions.question: What's unique about zebra stripes?

choices.label: They're all identical
reply: Nope. They just look it from far away.
Each zebra's stripe pattern is unique.
Blending in and standing out. At the same time.

choices.label: They change every morning
reply: Ha. That'd be exhausting.
Each zebra's pattern is unique and stays for life.
Some foals even recognize mom by her stripes.

choices.label: Every zebra's pattern is one of a kind
reply: Correct. Like fingerprints.
No two zebras share the exact same stripes.
Same herd, different stripes. Individuality. I like that.

questions.factBasis: Zebra stripe patterns are unique to individuals.

questions.scene: Rue looks up at a flock of birds outside, watching closely.
lines: I'm good. ...Teamwork question. Ugh. Fine.
questions.question: Why do geese fly in a V formation?

choices.label: Because V stands for 'victory'
reply: Cute. Wrong.
It saves energy. Birds take turns leading.
Rotating the lead means nobody burns out.

choices.label: To save energy, taking turns at the front
reply: Correct. Teamwork.
Birds behind ride the lead bird's air currents, and the lead role rotates.
Even the strongest one can't lead forever. ...I hate that I relate.

choices.label: To look cool in photos
reply: They do look cool. Not the reason.
The V helps them save energy, and they swap leaders.
Teamwork wins long distances.

questions.factBasis: Geese fly in V formation for aerodynamic efficiency, rotating the lead.

questions.scene: Rue raises one eyebrow, clearly debunking something in her head.
lines: This one annoys me. Every documentary gets it wrong.
questions.question: Is the 'alpha wolf' fighting for dominance how wild packs work?

choices.label: No, wild packs are families led by parents
reply: Correct. Myth busted.
The 'alpha' idea came from captive wolves, not wild families.
Even the scientist who popularized it later corrected it. Respect.

choices.label: Yes, wolves battle for the top spot
reply: Nope. Popular myth.
That idea came from studying unrelated wolves in captivity.
In the wild, packs are just families. Parents lead. That's it.

choices.label: Only on Tuesdays
reply: Ha. ...Funny. No.
Wild packs are families led by the parents.
The alpha myth came from captive wolves.

questions.factBasis: The 'alpha' dominance concept came from captive studies; wild packs are families (Mech later corrected it).

questions.scene: Rue shadowboxes once, very fast, then pretends she didn't.
lines: I'm good. ...This shrimp could beat me. I've accepted it.
questions.question: What's special about a mantis shrimp's punch?

choices.label: It's slow but very polite
reply: Opposite. Very rude. Very fast.
Its strike is among the fastest in nature.
It can crack aquarium glass. Aquariums hate this guy.

choices.label: It's one of the fastest strikes in the animal world
reply: Correct. Absurdly fast.
Its club can smash snail shells and even crack aquarium glass.
Small. Colorful. Will fight you. My spirit animal.

choices.label: It only punches when it's sad
reply: Ha. It punches whenever it wants.
It's one of the fastest strikes in nature.
Shells, glass, your confidence. All cracked.

questions.factBasis: Mantis shrimp strikes are among the fastest in nature and can crack aquarium glass.

questions.scene: Rue holds up a mushroom and narrows her eyes at it.
lines: I'm good. ...Mushrooms are weird. Hear this.
questions.question: Genetically, mushrooms are more closely related to...?

choices.label: Animals
reply: Correct. Wild, right?
Fungi split from the animal branch later than from plants.
I'm related to a mushroom. Don't tell Sky. He'll make it a nickname.

choices.label: Plants
reply: Everyone guesses that. Wrong.
Fungi are actually closer relatives of animals than plants.
So that mushroom is technically more my cousin than a tree is. Ugh.

choices.label: Rocks
reply: Ha. No. Rocks aren't alive. Usually.
Fungi are more closely related to animals than to plants.
Mushroom, you're family now. Unfortunately.

questions.factBasis: Fungi are more closely related to animals than plants (Opisthokonta).

questions.scene: Rue laughs at something on her phone, then quickly makes her face neutral again.
lines: I'm good. ...Saw a meme. Sky sent it. Whatever.
questions.question: What do studies suggest about couples who laugh together?

choices.label: They take each other less seriously
reply: Nope. The opposite, kind of.
Shared laughter is linked to feeling closer and more supported.
Laughing together is serious business. Ironically.

choices.label: It makes no difference
reply: It does. Science said so.
Couples who laugh together tend to feel closer.
Send the dumb meme. It counts.

choices.label: They tend to feel closer and more supported
reply: Correct. Shared laughter helps.
Couples who laugh together report feeling closer and more satisfied.
Sky makes me laugh. Don't tell him. He'll get cocky.

questions.factBasis: Kurtz & Algoe (2015): shared laughter associated with relationship closeness/satisfaction.

questions.scene: Rue dabs green paste on a cracker, bites it, and blinks very fast.
lines: I'm good. ...I'm good. That was not real wasabi.
questions.question: Most 'wasabi' served outside Japan is actually what?

choices.label: Pure grated wasabi root
reply: Rarely. Real wasabi is pricey.
Most is horseradish, mustard, and green coloring.
Real wasabi is notoriously hard to grow. Fussy plant.

choices.label: Horseradish with green coloring
reply: Correct. Imposter paste.
Real wasabi root is rare and expensive, so horseradish fills in.
Things aren't always what they say they are. Lesson.

choices.label: Mashed avocado with chili
reply: That's just spicy guacamole.
It's usually horseradish and mustard, colored green.
Trust no green paste. Ever.

questions.factBasis: Most 'wasabi' outside Japan is horseradish/mustard with coloring.

questions.scene: Rue leans on your wall. She looks like she doesn't care. She cares.
lines: Independence talk. My favorite topic. Kind of. Don't read into it.
questions.question: Weekends: some solo time, or always together?

choices.label: Some solo time
reply: Solo time. Same.
Space keeps me me.

choices.label: Always together
reply: Always together? Huh. That's... sweet.
Not me. But sweet.

A:A: Solo time for both of you. Good.
So you and {partner} trust each other enough to roam.
Then you come back with stories. That's the best part.
A:B: Always together for you. {partner} wants some solo time.
They're not leaving you. They're recharging. Different thing.
Give them one solo afternoon. They'll come back softer.
B:A: Solo time for you. {partner} wants always together.
They'll want Saturday plans. You'll want a solo hike.
Morning alone, afternoon together. Sky and I do that. It works.
B:B: Always together for both of you. Huh. Cute.
Honestly, {partner} and you are a pack of two. Inseparable.
I'd get claustrophobic. You two make it look nice. Annoying.

questions.scene: Rue checks her phone. Puts it away. Checks it again.
lines: Texting rules. Sky texts too much. I like it. Don't tell him.
questions.question: Staying in touch: a daily text, or only when there's news?

choices.label: A daily text
reply: Daily text. Alright. I get it.
A tiny 'hey' that says 'still here.'

choices.label: Only when there's news
reply: Only when there's news. Same.
No need to over-text.

A:A: Daily text for both of you. Alright, cute.
I can picture it: you and {partner} send one 'you good?' a day. Minimum.
Simple. Steady. I could get used to it. Maybe.
A:B: Only news for you. {partner} likes a daily text.
They're checking their phone. Waiting. For anything.
Send a one-word text. 'Good.' That's all. It counts.
B:A: Daily text for you. {partner} only texts with news.
You'll send 'hey.' They'll reply in three days with 'bought a plant.'
Send yours anyway. They read them. They smile.
B:B: Only news for both of you. Efficient.
Pretty sure you and {partner} trust the silence. Silence means all good.
Honestly? Peaceful. Respect.

questions.scene: Rue sharpens a pencil with a pocket knife. Unbothered. Mostly.
lines: I'm good. ...Recharging question. I have a method.
questions.question: To recharge: alone time, friends, or a long run?

choices.label: Alone time
reply: Alone time. Same.
Quiet is power.

choices.label: Friends
reply: Friends. Okay. Social.
A pack helps. ...Sometimes.

choices.label: A long run
reply: A long run. Obviously.
Miles fix most things.

A:A: Alone time for both of you. Respect.
Lowkey, {partner} and you probably recharge in separate rooms. Happily.
Then reunite fully charged. Efficient.
A:B: Friends for you. {partner} needs alone time.
You'll want to go out. They'll want the couch.
Invite a friend over. Let them hide in the bedroom. Peace.
A:C: A run for you. {partner} needs alone time.
Run solo. They rest solo. Then meet.
Best kind of together. Apart first.
B:A: Alone time for you. {partner} needs friends.
They'll be out. You'll be in. Fine.
Meet up after. Swap stories.
B:B: Friends for both of you. Social pack.
You and {partner} recharge with a crowd. I'd need a nap after.
But good for you. Seriously.
B:C: A run for you. {partner} needs friends.
Run to the party. Arrive sweaty. Iconic.
Or run in the morning, friends at night.
C:A: Alone time for you. {partner} goes for a run.
They run. You rest. Both recharging. Both quiet.
C:B: Friends for you. {partner} goes for a run.
Run with friends. Everyone wins. Mostly them.
Or meet at the finish line with snacks.
C:C: Long runs for both of you. Respect.
So {partner} and you probably run side by side without talking.

questions.scene: Rue struggles to open a jar. She doesn't ask for help. She keeps struggling.
lines: I've got it. I've got it. Okay.
questions.question: When you need help: ask right away, or try alone first?

choices.label: Ask right away
reply: Ask right away. Smart. Healthy.
No shame in it. ...I'm working on that.

choices.label: Try alone first
reply: Try alone first. Same.
Proving I can. Every time.

A:A: Ask right away for both of you. Great.
Honestly, you and {partner} just say 'can you help?' Easy.
Teach me. I'm still on the jar.
A:B: Try alone first for you. {partner} asks right away.
They'll hand you the jar. You'll want to do it yourself.
Let them help once. ...It's nice. Sky taught me.
B:A: Ask right away for you. {partner} tries alone first.
Offer help gently. Don't grab the jar.
Let them try. Then say 'want me to?' Quietly.
B:B: Try alone first for both of you. Same.
I can picture it: {partner} and you will struggle with the jar for ten minutes. Side by side.
Just pass it over eventually. Please.

questions.scene: Rue unfolds a paper map, upside down, then flips it.
lines: I know where we are. Mostly.
questions.question: Lost while driving: ask for directions, or figure it out yourself?

choices.label: Ask for directions
reply: Ask for directions. Efficient.
Less time lost. More time snacking.

choices.label: Figure it out
reply: Figure it out. Same.
Pride is a GPS.

A:A: Ask for directions for both of you. Smart.
Pretty sure you and {partner} will never circle the same roundabout four times.
Respect. Practical. Sky and I once drove an hour the wrong way. Proudly.
A:B: You figure it out. {partner} asks for directions.
They'll pull over. You'll sigh.
Let them ask. Arrive on time. Pride intact. Mostly.
B:A: You ask for directions. {partner} wants to figure it out.
They'll say 'I know where we are.' They don't.
Ask quietly. Let them think it was their idea.
B:B: Figure it out for both of you. Stubborn duo.
Lowkey, {partner} and you will drive in circles for an hour. Together.
At least the playlist is good.

questions.scene: Rue narrows her eyes at you, calculating something.
lines: I'm good. ...Stress question. I don't get stressed. Much.
questions.question: When stressed, what does your partner do?
questions.selfQuestion: When you're stressed, what do you do?

choices.label: Pulls away
reply: Pulls away. Same.
Distance feels safe.

choices.label: Leans in
reply: Leans in. Huh. Okay.
Closeness helps them.

choices.label: Cleans everything
reply: Cleans everything. Scrub therapy.
Shiny counters, calm brain.

A:A: Pulling away, and {partner} knew it.
They know your silence isn't about them.
Still. Tell them once in a while. Sky likes that.
A:B: You lean in. {partner} expected you to pull away.
They're giving you space. You want closeness.
Say it. 'Stay.' One word. Works.
A:C: You clean everything. {partner} expected you to pull away.
They're giving you space. You're scrubbing the oven.
Let them help. Or just let them watch. It's a show.
B:A: You pull away. {partner} expected you to lean in.
They're opening their arms. You're closing the door.
Tell them it's not about them. It's just how you process.
B:B: Leaning in, and {partner} knew it.
They know you need closeness when things get heavy.
Lucky. That's harder than it looks.
B:C: You clean everything. {partner} expected you to lean in.
They want a hug. You want the floors spotless.
Hug them with rubber gloves on. Compromise.
C:A: They're waiting for scrubbing sounds. You've gone quiet.
C:B: They're handing you a sponge. You want a hug.
Hug first. Clean later. Maybe never.
C:C: They know a spotless kitchen means a stressful week.
Help them scrub. Or bring snacks.

questions.scene: Rue folds her arms, watching you closely.
lines: Funny question coming. Ironic, given who's asking.
questions.question: When someone asks your partner 'you okay?', what do they say?
questions.selfQuestion: When someone asks you 'you okay?', what do you say?

choices.label: 'I'm good.' (They're not.)
reply: 'I'm good.' Classic. That's me.
Everyone's 'good.' Nobody's good.

choices.label: The honest truth
reply: The honest truth. Brave.
Rare. Respect.

A:A: 'I'm good,' and {partner} sees right through it.
They know 'I'm good' means 'ask again later.'
Sky does that. Asks twice. It works. Annoyingly.
A:B: You're honest. {partner} expected 'I'm good.'
They were ready to decode an 'I'm good.' You just told them the truth.
That's trust. It feels weird. Then it feels really good.
B:A: You say 'I'm good.' {partner} thought you'd be honest.
They're taking 'good' at face value. Uh oh.
Say one real thing next time. Just one.
B:B: The honest truth, and {partner} knew it.
They know you'll just tell them. No code.
Keep that. It's rare. Trust me.

questions.scene: Rue sneezes, then glares at you like you caused it.
lines: I'm not sick.
questions.question: When your partner gets sick, how do they act?
questions.selfQuestion: When you get sick, how do you act?

choices.label: 'I'm fine,' refuses all help
reply: Refuses help. Same.
'I'm fine,' while sneezing.

choices.label: Wants to be babied
reply: Wants to be babied. Honest.
Soup. Blankets. Attention.

A:A: Refusing help, and {partner} knew it.
They'll leave soup by the door. Silently.
That's how you handle a lone wolf. Respect.
A:B: You want babying. {partner} thought you'd refuse help.
They're giving you space. You want a blanket burrito.
Ask for soup. They'll be thrilled.
B:A: You refuse help. {partner} thought you'd want babying.
They're bringing soup. You're pretending you're fine.
Take the soup. Just the soup. That's a start.
B:B: Wanting to be babied, and {partner} knew it.
They've got the soup and the blanket ready.
Let them. It's nice. ...I think.

questions.scene: Rue pretends to check her nails, avoiding your eyes.
lines: I'm good. ...Missing someone question. Ugh.
questions.question: How does your partner say 'I missed you'?
questions.selfQuestion: How do you say 'I missed you'?

choices.label: A long hug
reply: A long hug. Huh. Sweet.
Arms say it. No words needed.

choices.label: Pretends they didn't
reply: Pretends they didn't. Same.
'Oh, you were gone?'

A:A: A long hug, and {partner} knew it.
They know you'll squeeze them for a full minute.
...That's nice. Don't tell anyone I said that.
A:B: You pretend you didn't miss them. {partner} expected a hug.
They're waiting with open arms. You're 'busy.'
Hug them. Just once. Then go back to pretending.
B:A: You hug long. {partner} thought you'd play it cool.
Surprise. Softie revealed.
They'll love it. Hug them extra long next time.
B:B: Pretending you didn't, and {partner} knew it.
They see you trying not to smile when they walk in.
You're not fooling anyone. Sky says the same about me.

questions.scene: Rue fixes your wobbly chair leg without being asked, then shrugs.
lines: Taking care of people. Not my thing. Obviously.
questions.question: How does your partner take care of you?
questions.selfQuestion: How do you take care of your partner?

choices.label: Fixes practical stuff
reply: Fixes stuff. Practical love.
Squeaky door? Gone. Leaky faucet? Fixed.

choices.label: Shows up with food
reply: Shows up with food. Classic.
Love is a warm meal.

A:A: Fixing things, and {partner} knew it.
They know a fixed shelf is your 'I love you.'
Same. I fix stuff for Sky. He knows what it means.
A:B: You bring food. {partner} thought you'd fix stuff.
They're expecting a toolbox. You arrive with lasagna.
Better surprise, honestly. Way better.
B:A: You fix stuff. {partner} thought you'd bring food.
They're waiting for soup. You're fixing the faucet.
Tell them the faucet is a love letter. Plumbing romance.
B:B: Showing up with food, and {partner} knew it.
They know dinner on the doorstep means you care.
Food is love. No argument.
